been tabulated to compare with those of Duncan (1981).
Themostcomprehensiveanalysisofplatemotionstodateis
arguablythatofDoubrovine,Steinberger,andTorsvik(2012),
who investigated the effects of moving hot spots and devel-
oped the global moving hot spot reference frame. For times
younger than 50 Ma the motions are essentially the same as
for Torsvik, Mu€ller, Van der Voo, Steinberger, and Gaina
(2008), which we use below. Thus, for late Cenozoic times, a
fixed or moving hot spot frame makes very little difference.
Doubrovine et al. (2012, table 4) shows that the net rotation
of the lithosphere is less than 0.2(cid:1)/Ma back to 50 Ma. For 20
Maevents,themaximumerrorwemightexpectis4(cid:1) incom-
paring the North American and Australian pole paths, which
is less than the A confidence limit of the Australian pole
95
positions.
